summary: A TechCrunch report on how the war that followed Hamas' attacks on Israelis is affecting Israel's startup ecosystem, which is a major part of the country's economy. Founders, investors and PR people describe reservist call-ups affecting 10-30% of tech workers, a gradual return to work, and the need to keep businesses running to sustain the economy. Investors such as OurCrowd's Jon Medved and GGV's Oren Yunger expressed confidence in the sector's long-term resilience, though funding was already down sharply before the attacks.
one_line: Israeli startups and investors adapt to war with mass reservist call-ups and disrupted work, while insisting the tech sector will stay resilient.
key_facts: In 2022, technology contributed more than 18% of Israel's GDP, the most of any single sector, per the Israel Innovation Authority's annual report.
About 14% of Israeli citizens work in high tech, roughly 1.3 million people in a country of 9.2 million.
Israel has 9,000 active startups, third-highest in the world after the Bay Area and NYC, which brought in $95 billion in venture capital over the last five years.
Startups and larger tech companies exported $71 billion last year, 48.3% of all exports across industries.
Funding in Israel dropped 73% to a provisional $3.2 billion in the first half of 2023 versus the same period in 2022, according to IVC data.
An estimated 10% to 30% of Israel's tech employees are being mobilized, and more than 500 VCs have pledged support for Israeli startups.
Lazer Cohen of Concrete Media said 10-25% of Israeli team members at his clients and agency have been called up to reserve duty.
Kfir ben Shooshan of Inokim estimated that at least 10% of citizens have enlisted or volunteered for the army.
The tech industry had led opposition to the government's judicial reform bid, which was halted as both sides united against the larger threat.
For most Israeli startups the customer base is global and go-to-market teams are often in the U.S., so the war may slow product development but not directly hit short-term sales.
Jon Medved of OurCrowd said that within a year or more Israel's tech ecosystem will emerge from the war stronger, bigger, with more investment and returns.
Oren Yunger of GGV said he is 100% sure that none of his firm's Israeli portfolio companies will go bust as a result of the war.
